---
name: Genuine Ihara boundary
description: Why the finite genuine-form predicate cannot by itself prove restricted Ihara injectivity.
---

Finite support, Hecke stability, and exclusion of the raw infinite-support
`(-Bp 1, 1)` cancellation witness do not rule out every relation between the
two degeneracy expansions. Keep the missing pair-level q-expansion/Ihara input
explicit, and derive restricted kernel-zero from that supplied proposition.

**Why:** A principal module generated by the coefficient sequence supported
only at index zero satisfies the finite genuine-form boundary but contains a
nonzero cancellation pair because its `Bp` image is itself. Thus promoting the
single-witness exclusion to full injectivity would be false.

**How to apply:** On each enriched descent edge, carry an inspectable
proposition excluding all nonzero `a + Bp b = 0` relations in the supplied
genuine submodule. Derive the restricted Ihara hypothesis at the use site
without choice; do not claim the geometric proposition has been proved.
